name: Ra.One
summary: A self-learning video-game villain who breaks out into the real world to hunt the boy who nearly beat him. Played by Arjun Rampal in Ra.One (2011).
origin: Game designer Shekhar Subramaniam builds a new game for his son Prateek and, on Prateek's suggestion, makes the villain stronger than the hero. Ra.One is faceless, can shapeshift and read minds, runs on self-learning AI, and draws its power from a device called the H.A.R.T. When Prateek, playing as Lucifer, leaves their match unfinished, Ra.One uses new technology that lets digital objects enter the real world, escapes, and kills to track Lucifer down, Shekhar included. The name riffs on Ravana.
powers: Powered by a H.A.R.T.; without it he weakens but cannot be killed

storyline.title: Unfinished game
storyline.beat: Ra.One escapes into the real world, murders the game's motion-capture artist Akashi and then Shekhar while hunting Lucifer.

storyline.title: Shattered into cubes
storyline.beat: G.One arrives and sets off a gas explosion that breaks Ra.One apart and leaves him without his H.A.R.T.

storyline.title: Hostage game
storyline.beat: Rebuilt, Ra.One hypnotises Prateek's mother Sonia, takes her form, kidnaps Prateek, and sends the real Sonia on a runaway train toward CST station.

storyline.title: Ten Ra.Ones
storyline.beat: He multiplies into ten copies, but only the real one casts a shadow. G.One shoots its H.A.R.T. and destroys it.

gossip.text: With a budget of about ₹150 crore including publicity, Ra.One was the most expensive Indian film ever made at the time.
The film won the National Film Award for Best Special Effects.
The final clue: of the ten Ra.One copies, only the real one casts a shadow.
Jackie Chan was approached to play Akashi but turned it down.
It opened in India on 26 October 2011, right on Diwali.

quiz.q: What gives Ra.One and G.One their power?
quiz.why: Both characters run on a device called the H.A.R.T.

quiz.q: How does Prateek spot the real Ra.One among the copies?
quiz.why: Only the real Ra.One has a shadow.
Arjun Rampal played the title villain.

theme.tagline: Player quit mid-match? He came out to finish the level in person.

timeline.title: Out of the game
timeline.note: Arjun Rampal plays the video-game villain who breaks into the real world in the film released on 26 October 2011.

timeline.title: Tie-in video game
timeline.note: Ra.One – The Game lands on PS2 and PS3 a few weeks ahead of the film.

timeline.title: Ten copies, one shadow
timeline.note: In the final level G.One spots the real Ra.One by his shadow and destroys his H.A.R.T.

timeline.title: National Award for VFX
timeline.note: The film wins Best Special Effects at the 59th National Film Awards for Red Chillies VFX.

timeline.title: Sequel talk
timeline.note: Shah Rukh Khan says any follow-up would be called G.One. It has not been made.
